panel.introduction: Varda is a distant binary-system primary whose outline was measured as it eclipsed a star. Its companion’s orbit helps orient this model, but Varda’s depth remains uncertain.

facts.label: Rotation
facts.value: Unresolved; photometric aliases and synchronous rotation remain alternatives

moreFacts.label: Shape interpretation
moreFacts.value: One published allowable triaxial model, with semiaxes 389, 353 and 248 km. The line-of-sight depth is unconstrained; these best-fit values illustrate a solution rather than a uniquely measured body shape.

controls.label: Shape model
controls.description: One published allowable triaxial model, with semiaxes 389, 353 and 248 km. The line-of-sight depth is unconstrained; these best-fit values illustrate a solution rather than a uniquely measured body shape. Assumes the spin pole aligns with Ilmarë’s orbit: J2000 RA 272.6° and declination −10.8°. This is a model prior; rotational phase and meridian are illustrative. The grid marks unmapped terrain.
controls.title: Published triaxial example model
